item.title: Volkswagen-Powered Death Race 2000 “Monster” Re-Creation
item.description: This fiberglass-bodied roadster is a re-creation of the “Monster” vehicle featured in the 1975 film Death Race 2000. Built more than two decades ago, it was among the collection of the Volo Auto Museum in Illinois in the early 2000s and spent time in a private collection before being displayed at the Rodz and Bodz museum in Colorado. item.title: 47k-Mile 2007 Honda S2000
item.description: This 2007 Honda S2000 remained registered with the initial owner in New Jersey until 2025, and it now has 47k miles. The car is finished in Silverstone Metallic over red and black leather and is powered by a 2.2-liter VTEC inline-four linked to a six-speed manual transmission and a limited-slip differential. item.title: 1967 Pontiac GTO Convertible
item.description: This 1967 Pontiac GTO convertible was acquired by the owner in the early 2000s, and it is powered by a 400ci V8 paired with a three-speed automatic transmission. item.title: 1996 Porsche 911 Turbo
item.description: This 1996 Porsche 911 Turbo was specified in Arena Red Metallic over Classic Grey leather upholstery, and it now shows 47k miles. item.title: 1953 Ford F-100 5-Speed
item.description: This 1953 Ford F-100 pickup was acquired by the previous owner in 2006 and was the subject of a multi-year refurbishment that was completed circa 2017. It is powered by a 239ci flathead V8 linked with a T5 five-speed manual transmission. item.title: 5k-Mile 2001 Acura NSX-T 6-Speed at No Reserve
item.description: This 2001 Acura NSX-T is a Spa Yellow Pearl-finished example that shows 5k miles and was previously sold on BaT in May 2024 and again in October 2025 prior to being reacquired by the selling dealer. Power is provided by a 3.2-liter DOHC V6 paired with a six-speed manual transaxle, and the cabin houses power-adjustable seats trimmed in Onyx leather. item.title: This Week’s Weird and Wonderful—December 12, 2025
item.description: Welcome to the Weekly Weird & Wonderful—our bi-fortnightly collection of the coolest, strangest, and most interesting cars currently on BaT. item.title: One-Family-Owned 1965 Porsche 356SC Coupe at No Reserve
item.description: This 1965 Porsche 356SC coupe was built on March 15, 1965 and delivered new to Vasek Polak of Manhattan Beach, California, where it was purchased new by the current owner's father. It is powered by a 1.6-liter flat-four paired with a four-speed manual transaxle and is finished in black over black leather. item.title: 5,400-Mile 2005 Lamborghini Murcielago Coupe 6-Speed
